title: Dispatch: canonical closure roster, pack-independent authority, closed hook relation (attempt 8)
description:
Fresh full review of PR #476 at 6a1b275: four P1, one P2. All remain inside
previously identified invariant classes, so NO rescope is required and a
FIX-VERIFICATION review is permitted next PROVIDED THE CONTRACT DOES NOT CHANGE.
Implement the existing invariants correctly; add no new invariant classes. If you
think the contract must change, report it rather than changing it.

TWO OF THESE PASSED SUPERVISOR REVIEW AND SHOULD NOT HAVE. Read F1 and F4 with
that in mind — the bar is higher than 'a test exists'.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.md
  packages/core/src/rules/findingRegistry.ts
  packages/core/test/findingRegistry.test.ts

=== F1 (P1): CLOSURE ACCEPTS AN OBLIGATION SUBSET ===
The committed test builds validFixture = registry.rows.filter(derived) — a
4-row subset — and asserts closure READY. The closure API validates only rows
that are PRESENT, so DELETING the 64 unresolved obligations produces green
closure. That is the cheapest possible way to fake closure and the gate permits
it. (The supervisor reviewed this exact fixture and called it valid. It is not.)

FIX: closure must validate against the CANONICAL obligation set, not against
whatever rows happen to be present. Commit a canonical row roster — the same
device that fixed the equivalent hole in the capability ledger — and make a
registry missing any canonical row report those rows as BLOCKERS. Test that
deleting rows increases blockers rather than clearing them.

=== F2 (P1): THE FOUR 'DERIVED' ROWS ARE DEFINED BY THE PACK UNDER REPAIR ===
Rule, spell, half-damage and engine-capability membership is generated from
current records, text, readiness states and hooks. An obligation already OMITTED
from the pack is absent from both the generated set and the stored snapshot, so
it is invisible in exactly the case the registry exists to catch. This
contradicts the contract's own rule that a row's authority may not be the pack
under repair.

FIX: a row may be 'derived' only when its authority is established INDEPENDENTLY
of the pack — from source or from an audit finding's own recorded scope — with
the pack query supplying CURRENT membership to be compared against that
authority. Where independent authority cannot be established, the row is
'underived'.
EXPECT THE DERIVED COUNT TO FALL, possibly to zero. If all 68 rows end
underived, that is an ACCEPTABLE AND HONEST outcome: this PR's value is the
model, the gate and a truthful status, not a derived count. Do NOT retain a row
as derived merely because a pack query returns something.

=== F3 (P1): CAPABILITY ASSIGNMENT IS HEURISTIC ===
primitiveForHook() lowercases the hook and keyword-matches with broad defaults,
so unknown or unrelated hook names receive valid primitives. The engine:F2
legendary-action primitive is not reachable through ANY branch.
FIX: replace it with a CLOSED hook-to-primitive relation. An unknown hook must
fail or resolve to an explicit unmapped state — never a guessed primitive. Make
the F2 legendary-action primitive reachable and test it. Add negative tests for
unknown and unrelated hook names.

=== F4 (P1): THE ANTI-TEMPLATE GUARD STILL ACCEPTS THE CHECKED-IN TEMPLATE ===
The normalizer removes literal titles and identifiers only. The checked-in
reasons and invariants share sentence SKELETONS with PARAPHRASED subjects, which
survive normalization and read as unique.

THE SUPERVISOR'S OWN REGRESSION TEST IS PART OF THE PROBLEM: it constructs two
rows whose reason text is byte-identical apart from an interpolated title. The
guard already caught that case. The test therefore proved nothing about the
pattern actually present in the data, and passing it created false confidence.

FIX:
 * Strengthen normalization to collapse paraphrased subject noun phrases, not
   just literal titles and IDs — compare structural skeletons after removing
   content words, or require measurable divergence (n-gram or edit-distance)
   between rows' residuals.
 * The new negative test must use THE ACTUAL CHECKED-IN PATTERN — same skeleton,
   paraphrased subject — as its failing case. A test that only catches
   byte-identical text is not sufficient.
 * Then REWRITE THE DATA the strengthened guard catches. Expect many rows to
   need genuinely distinct text. Do not relax the guard to fit the data; that is
   the failure this has now repeated four times in this program.

=== F5 (P2): FORBIDDEN TOTALS BYPASS VALIDATION INSIDE ARRAYS ===
hasForbiddenTotal() begins 'if (!isObject(value)) return;', so an array returns
immediately and nested count/total fields inside members or capability catalogs
are never inspected. FIX: recurse into arrays; add a test with a forbidden total
nested inside an array member.

=== PRESERVE ===
The durable obligation/target/invariant vs violation split; 68 rows and 70
aliases each resolving once; qualified engine capability targets from
eshyra-o9bd.19.1.9; exact structured identities; the fail-closed blocker-identity
assertions.

=== ENVIRONMENT / CONSTRAINTS ===
npm ci first; npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing. Edit only the four files
above. A sibling dispatch runs in parallel on PR #477. Do not touch package.json,
internal.ts, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .github/, or any script/CI file. Do not
regenerate the pack or run the importer. Do not modify any bead but your own; no
bd dolt push; no push, PR comment, or merge. The PR body is the supervisor's to
fix, after the push.
acceptance_criteria:
• Closure validates against a canonical row roster; deleting rows increases blockers rather than clearing them, with a test.
• A row is derived only with authority independent of the pack under repair; the derived count is allowed to fall to zero.
• primitiveForHook is a closed relation; unknown hooks fail or resolve unmapped; the engine:F2 legendary-action primitive is reachable and tested.
• The anti-template guard catches same-skeleton paraphrased-subject text, proven by a test using the actual checked-in pattern; caught data is rewritten rather than the guard relaxed.
• hasForbiddenTotal recurses into arrays, with a test for a total nested in an array member.
• Contract unchanged so fix-verification review remains permissible.
• npm run verify:worktree passes.
